Surah al-Hujurat is Madani. [Al-Suyuti cites in ad-Durr al-Manthur (7/546), from Ibn ad-Daris, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: "Surah al-Hujurat was revealed in Medina."]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] forward before Allah and His Messenger.﴾ Ya'qub read "lā tuqaddamū" with a fatha on the ta' and the dal, from the taqaddum (going forward), meaning "do not go forward." The others read it with a damma on the ta' and a kasra on the dal, from the taqdim (putting forward). It is intransitive here, with the meaning of taqaddum. [Abu Ubayda said:] The Arabs say, "Do not go forward before the imam and before the father," meaning do not hasten ahead with a command or prohibition without him. The meaning of "between the two hands" is "in front," i.e., do not put yourselves forward before their command and their prohibition.

Scholars differed on its meaning. Al-Sha'bi narrated from Jabir that it concerns slaughtering on the day of al-Adha, and this is also the view of al-Hasan: do not slaughter before the Prophet (ﷺ) slaughters. This is because some people slaughtered before the Prophet's (ﷺ) prayer, so he ordered them to repeat the slaughter. [Narrated by al-Tabari (26/117) and Abd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir (2/230). Al-Suyuti in ad-Durr al-Manthur (7/547) also attributes it to Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir. It should be noted that this contradicts the authentic chains concerning the occasion of revelation of the verse, so the statements of al-Hasan and Jabir fall under the general meaning of the verse and are not its cause of revelation.]

Al-Malihi informed us: Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi, who said: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il said: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, who said: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Yazid, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Bara', who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) addressed us on the day of al-Nahr, and said: "The first thing we begin with on this day of ours is to pray, then we return and slaughter. Whoever does this has followed our sunnah. And whoever slaughters before we pray, it is merely meat he has hastened for his family; it has nothing to do with the sacrifice." [Narrated by al-Bukhari, in the chapter on the Eid sermon after the Eid (2/453).]

It was also narrated by Masruq from Aisha that it concerns the prohibition of fasting on the day of doubt [see al-Kafi al-Shafi p. (155)], meaning: do not fast before your Prophet fasts.

Al-Malihi informed us: Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi, who said: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il said: Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, who said: Hisham ibn Yusuf narrated to us that Ibn Juraij informed them, from Ibn Abi Mulayka, that Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr informed them that a caravan from Bani Tamim came to the Prophet (ﷺ). Abu Bakr said: "Appoint al-Qa'qa' ibn Ma'bad ibn Zurara." Umar said: "Rather, appoint al-Aqra' ibn Habis." Abu Bakr said: "You only intend to oppose me." Umar said: "I did not intend to oppose you." They argued until their voices were raised, and on account of that the verse was revealed: "O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] forward before Allah and His Messenger," until its end. [Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, chapter on "Indeed those who call you from behind the chambers, most of them do not reason" (8/592), and in al-Maghazi, and in al-I'tisam bil-Kitab wal-Sunnah.]

Nafi' also narrated it from Ibn Abi Mulayka, who said: the verse was revealed: "O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet," up to His words, "a great reward." He added: Ibn al-Zubayr said: After this verse, Umar would not speak to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) except in the manner of asking him to clarify, and he did not mention it from his father, meaning Abu Bakr. [Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, chapter on "Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet," (8/590).]

Qatadah said: The verse was revealed concerning people who would say, "If only such-and-such had been revealed," or "such-and-such had been done," and Allah disliked that.

Mujahid said: Do not act presumptuously against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in anything until Allah decides it through his tongue. [Narrated by al-Tabari (26/116). Al-Suyuti in ad-Durr al-Manthur (7/547) adds attribution to Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman. See also al-Bahr al-Muhit (8/105), al-Qurtubi (16/301).]

Al-Dahhak said: meaning in fighting and in the laws of the religion: do not decide a matter apart from Allah and His Messenger.

﴿And fear Allah﴾ by neglecting His right and opposing His command, ﴿indeed Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of your statements, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of your actions.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 49, verse 2:

﴿O you who believe, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, nor speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another﴾ He commanded them to honour him, to revere him, and not to raise their voices in his presence, nor to call out to him as some of them call out to others. ﴿Lest your deeds should be nullified﴾ meaning, lest your good deeds be nullified. It is also said: for fear that your good deeds would be nullified, ﴿while you do not perceive﴾.

Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir related to us, 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi related to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan related to us, Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj related to us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah related to us, al-Hasan ibn Musa related to us, Hammad ibn Salamah related to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When this verse was revealed, "O you who believe, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet," and so on, Thabit ibn Qays sat in his house and said: "I am among the people of the Fire." He withheld himself from the Prophet (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) asked Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, saying: "O Abu 'Amr, what is the matter with Thabit? Is he unwell?" Sa'd said: "He is my neighbour, and I know of no illness he has." Anas said: So Sa'd came to him and mentioned to him the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Thabit said: "This verse has been revealed, and you know that I am among the loudest of you in voice before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so I am among the people of the Fire." Sa'd mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rather, he is among the people of Paradise." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, chapter: "Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet," the verse, 8/590, and Muslim in Iman, chapter: The believer's fear that his deeds may be nullified, no. (119), 1/110.]]

It is also related that when this verse was revealed, Thabit sat on the road weeping. 'Asim ibn 'Adi passed by him and said: "What makes you weep, O Thabit?" He said: "This verse. I fear that it was revealed concerning me, and I am a man of loud voice. I fear that my deeds will be nullified and that I will be among the people of the Fire." 'Asim went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and weeping overcame Thabit. He went to his wife, Jamilah bint 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and said to her: "When I enter the stable of my horse, fasten the iron ring on me with a nail," and he said: "I will not leave until Allah causes me to die or the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is pleased with me." 'Asim came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him of the matter. He said to him: "Go and call him." 'Asim came to the place where he had seen him, but did not find him. He went to his family and found him in the horse's stable. He said to him: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is calling you." Thabit said: "Break the ring," so he broke it, and the two of them came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What makes you weep, O Thabit?" He said: "I am loud-voiced, and I fear that this verse was revealed concerning me." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Are you not content to live praiseworthy, to be killed as a martyr, and to enter Paradise?" He said: "I am content with the good news of Allah and His Messenger, and I will never raise my voice above the voice of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) again." Then Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 49, verse 3:

﴿Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah﴾ [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 26/118, and by Ibn Mardawayh through the route of Zayd ibn al-Habbab. Ibn Sa'd also narrated it with a sound chain; see Fath al-Bari: 6/620-621.]] . [The rest of the verse.]

Anas said: "We used to look at a man of the people of Paradise walking among us. When the Day of Yamama came, in the battle against Musaylima the Liar, Thabit saw some breaking among the Muslims, and a group of them fled. He said, 'Uff (shame) on these people!' Then Thabit said to Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfa: 'We never fought the enemies of Allah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) like this.' Then the two stood firm and fought until they were both killed. Thabit was martyred while wearing his armour. A man from among the Companions saw him after his death in a dream, and he said to him: 'Know that so-and-so, a man from the Muslims, took my armour and went off with it. It is in a corner of the camp beside a small horse tethered at its rope, and he has placed a cooking pot over my armour. Go to Khalid ibn al-Walid and inform him, so that he may recover my armour. And go to Abu Bakr, the Caliph of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and tell him: I owe a debt, which must be paid, and so-and-so, one of my slaves, is free.' The man informed Khalid, and he found the armour and the horse exactly as he had described. He recovered the armour, and Khalid informed Abu Bakr of that dream, and Abu Bakr carried out his bequest." [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad: 3/137; by Abd ibn Humayd: pp. 363-364; by Ibn Sa'd, al-Tabarani and al-Hakim, through the narration of Hammad ibn Abi Salama from Thabit. al-Hakim also narrated the story of the armour and the bequest in a longer form through another route from Thabit ibn Qays. See Fath al-Bari: 6/52. Ibn Hajar mentioned it in al-Matalib al-'Aliya: 4/120 and attributed it to Abu Ya'la. al-Busiri said: "Its origin is in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Anas." See also Ibn Kathir: 4/207, and Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq: 2/230.]]

Malik ibn Anas said: "I do not know of any bequest that was carried out after the death of its maker except this one."

Abu Hurayra and Ibn 'Abbas said: "When this verse was revealed, Abu Bakr would not speak to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) except in the manner of one who speaks in a whisper (ka-akhi al-sirar)." [[Narrated by al-Hakim: 2/462, who said: "This is a sound hadith according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not include it." al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/548 to Abd ibn Humayd and to al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman. See also Fath al-Bari: 8/591, and Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/108.]]

Ibn al-Zubayr said: "When this verse was revealed, 'Umar did not speak to the Prophet (ﷺ) after that without the Prophet (ﷺ) having to ask him to repeat what he said, because of how low his voice was. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who lower their voices﴾ [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Tafsir, chapter "Do not raise your voices..." 8/590.]] , that is, they lower their voices ﴿in the presence of the Messenger of Allah﴾ out of reverence for him. ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety﴾, that is, He has examined them and purified them, just as gold is tested by fire so that its pure part comes out. ﴿For them is forgiveness and a great reward.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*), on surah 49, verses 4–5:

﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the private chambers (al-hujurat)...﴾ The common reciters (al-'ammah) read *al-hujurat* with a *ḍamma* on the *jīm*. Abu Ja'far read it with a *fatḥa* on the *jīm*. Both are dialectal variants (*lughatān*). The word is the plural of *al-ḥujar*, and *al-ḥujar* is the plural of *al-ḥujrah*, so it is a plural of a plural (*jam' al-jam'*).

Ibn 'Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a detachment (*sariyyah*) to Banu al-'Anbar and appointed 'Uyaynah ibn Hisn al-Fazari over them. When they learned that he was heading towards them, they fled and left their dependants behind. 'Uyaynah ibn Hisn took them captive and brought them to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Afterwards their men came to ransom the captives (*yafdūna al-dharārī*). They arrived at midday and found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) resting (*qā'ilan*) in his household. When the captives saw them, they cried out (*ajhashū*) to their fathers, weeping. Each of the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had a chamber (*ḥujrah*) [...] [[The words between the brackets are omitted in "a".]], so they hurried for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to come out to them. They began calling out: "O Muhammad, come out to us!" until they woke him from his sleep. He came out to them, and they said: "O Muhammad, free our dependants for us (*fādinā ʿiyālanā*)!" Then Jibril (peace be upon him) descended and said: "Allah commands you to appoint a man between you and them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Are you content for Sabrah ibn 'Amr, who is upon your religion, to be the arbiter between me and you?" They said: "Yes." Sabrah said: "I will not judge between them unless my paternal uncle is present as a witness, and he is al-A'war ibn Bashamah." They agreed to him. Al-A'war said: "I think you should ransom half of them and free the other half." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am content." So he ransomed half of them and freed the other half. Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the private chambers, most of them do not understand.﴾ He described them with ignorance and lack of intellect.

[[See: *al-Kafi al-Shafi*, p. (156).]]

﴿And if they had been patient until you come out to them, it would have been better for them.﴾ Muqatil said: It would have been better for them because you would have freed all of them and released them without ransom. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.﴾

Qatadah said: It was revealed concerning some Bedouins (*a'rāb*) of Banu Tamim who came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and called out at the door.

[[Narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq in *al-Tafsir*: 2/230. See also al-Tabari: 26/122; *Sirah* of Ibn Hisham: 2/516.]]

This is also related from Jabir, who said: The Banu Tamim came and called out at the door: "Come out to us, O Muhammad, for our praise is an adornment and our blame is a disgrace." The Prophet (ﷺ) came out saying: "Rather, that is Allah, whose praise is an adornment and whose blame is a disgrace." They said: "We are people of Banu Tamim. We have come with our poets and orators to contend with you in poetry and boasting." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I was not sent with poetry, nor was I commanded to boast. But bring forth [your case]." A young man from among them stood and recounted his own merit and that of his people. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who was the orator of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Stand and answer him." He answered him. Then their poet stood and recited some verses, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Hassan ibn Thabit: "Answer him," and he answered him. Then al-Aqra' ibn Habis stood and said: "Indeed Muhammad is one who is supported (*lamu'tan lah*). By Allah, I do not know this matter. Our orator spoke and their orator's speech was better, and our poet spoke and their poet was more eloquent and his speech was better." Then he drew near to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "What was before this will not harm you." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave them gifts and clothed them. 'Amr ibn al-Ahtam had stayed behind with their mounts because of his young age, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave him the same as he had given them. Some of them belittled him, the voices rose, and the uproar (*al-laghaṭ*) increased in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Concerning them was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet...﴾ the four verses, up to His words: ﴿Forgiving, Merciful.﴾

[[Narrated by al-Wahidi with his chain in *Asbab al-Nuzul*, p. (447). The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in *al-Kafi al-Shafi*, p. (156): "al-Tha'labi cited it through the route of Ya'la ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, from 'Umar ibn al-Hakam, from Jabir, 'Banu Tamim came and entered...' and mentioned it at length. The first part of it was narrated by al-Tirmidhi: 9/152–153, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, and he said: 'This is a hasan gharib hadith.' Imam Ahmad narrated it: 3/488, from al-Aqra' ibn Habis. Al-Haythami in *al-Majma'*: 7/108 narrated it from al-Aqra' ibn Habis and said: 'Ahmad and al-Tabarani narrated it, and one of the two chains of Ahmad has narrators who are those of the Sahih, if Abu Salamah heard from al-Aqra'; otherwise it is mursal like Ahmad's other chain.']]

Zayd ibn Arqam said: Some people from among the Arabs came to the Prophet (ﷺ). Some of them said to others: "Let us go to this man. If he is a prophet, we are the happiest of people with him; and if he is a king, we will live in his shade." They came and began calling out: "O Muhammad! O Muhammad!" So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the private chambers, most of them do not understand. And if they had been patient until you come out to them, it would have been better for them. And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.﴾

Al-Haythami in *al-Majma'*: (7/108) said: "al-Tabarani narrated it, and in its chain is Dawud ibn Rashid al-Tafawi, whom Ibn Hibban considered trustworthy and Ibn Ma'in considered weak." See also: *al-Durr al-Manthur*: 7/552–553; al-Qurtubi: 16/309.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 49, verse 6:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, if there comes to you a defiantly disobedient person with information, investigate it carefully﴾ and the rest of the verse. It was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'it, whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent to the Banu al-Mustaliq after the battle as a collector of zakat (sadaqat). There had been enmity between him and them in the Jahiliyyah. When the people heard of him, they went out to meet him, honouring the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Satan whispered to him that they intended to kill him, so he became afraid of them and returned from the road to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "The Banu al-Mustaliq have withheld their sadaqat and intended to kill me." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry and resolved to make war on them. The people learned of his return, so they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we heard of your messenger and went out to meet him, to honour him and to pay him what we had gathered of the right of Allah, exalted is He. Then it seemed to him that he should return, and we feared that he only turned back from the road because of a letter that came to him from you concerning an anger you had against us. We seek refuge in Allah from His anger and the anger of His Messenger." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then suspected them, and he sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to them secretly with an army, and ordered him to conceal his arrival from them, and said to him: "Look, and if you see from them what indicates their faith, take from them the zakat of their wealth; but if you do not see that, then deal with them as one deals with disbelievers." Khalid did so, and he came upon them and heard from them the adhan for the Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers. He took their sadaqat, and he saw from them nothing but obedience and goodness. He returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him of the report, so Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, if there comes to you a defiantly disobedient person﴾, meaning al-Walid ibn Uqbah [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 26/123, Imam Ahmad: 4/279, and 'Abd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir: 2/231. Ibn Kathir said: 4/209-210, "Many exegetes mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'it when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him over the zakat of the Banu al-Mustaliq, and this has been related through several routes, and among the best of them is what Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad from the report of the king of the Banu al-Mustaliq, who was al-Harith ibn Abi Dirar..." then he related the hadith and related other reports... And al-Haythami said: 7/111, "al-Tabarani narrated it, and in its chain is Musa ibn 'Ubaydah, who is weak."]] ﴿with information﴾: with news. ﴿investigate it carefully﴾: that you may ﴿not harm﴾ by killing and fighting ﴿a people﴾ who are innocent ﴿out of ignorance, and then become regretful for what you have done﴾: for having struck them by mistake.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 49, verse 7:**

﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah﴾. So fear Allah, lest you say something false or deny him, for Allah informs him of your states and makes him aware of them, and you would be exposed. ﴿Were he to obey you﴾, i.e. the Messenger, ﴿in much of the matter﴾, of what you inform him of, so that he judges according to your opinion, ﴿you would surely be in distress﴾, i.e. you would sin and be destroyed. Al-'anat (distress) means sin and destruction.

﴿But Allah has made faith beloved to you﴾, so He made it the most beloved of religions to you, ﴿and has made it appealing﴾, i.e. made it good, ﴿in your hearts﴾, until you chose it, and obey the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). ﴿And has made disbelief, defiance and disobedience hateful to you﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "He means lying." ﴿And disobedience﴾ means all the sins of Allah. Then he turned from address to narration and said: ﴿They are the rightly guided﴾, i.e. those who are guided.

[Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 49, verses 8–9]

﴿Bounty﴾, meaning this was a bounty ﴿from God and a favour, and God is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿If two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them﴾, to the end of the verse.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us; Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il [al-Bukhari] narrated to us; [135/b] Musaddad narrated to us; Mu'tamir narrated to us, saying: I heard my father say: Anas said: It was said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "If only you would go to Abd Allah ibn Ubayy." So the Prophet (ﷺ) set out to him, riding a donkey, and the Muslims set out walking with him. The land was salty. When the Prophet (ﷺ) reached him, [Abd Allah] said: "Keep away from me! By God, the stench of your donkey has harmed me." A man from the Ansar among them said: "By God, the donkey of the Messenger of God is better smelling than you." Then a man from [Abd Allah's] people became angry on his behalf, and they insulted each other. Each one's companions became angry for him, and there was striking among them with palm stalks, hands and sandals. We were informed that it was then revealed: "And if two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them."

[Commentary: It was narrated that when it was revealed, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited it, and they reconciled, and some of them refrained from others.]

Qatada said: It was revealed concerning two men from the Ansar who had a dispute over a right between them. One of them said to the other: "I will certainly take my right from you by force," relying on the large number of his kinsmen. The other called him to bring their case before the Prophet of God (ﷺ), but he refused to follow him. The matter remained between them until they pushed each other and some of them struck others with hands and sandals, though there was no fighting with swords.

Sufyan related from al-Suddi: There was a woman from the Ansar called Umm Zayd, who was married to a man, and something had happened between her and her husband. He took her up to an upper room and confined her. This reached her people, and they came, and his people came, and they fought with hands and sandals. Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "And if two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them," by calling them to the judgement of the Book of God and to accepting what it contains, in their favour and against them.

﴿But if one of them transgresses against the other﴾, meaning one of them oversteps against the other and refuses to accept the judgement of the Book of God, ﴿then fight the one that transgresses until it returns﴾, meaning returns, ﴿to the command of God﴾ in His Book, ﴿and if it returns﴾, meaning returns to the truth, ﴿then make peace between them with justice﴾, by bringing them to fairness and to acceptance of God's judgement, ﴿and act justly﴾, meaning be equitable, ﴿indeed God loves those who act justly﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 49, verse 10:

﴿Indeed, the believers are but brothers﴾ in religion and allegiance, ﴿so make reconciliation between your two brothers﴾ when they dispute and fight. Ya'qub read "bayna ikhwatikum" (between your brothers) with a ta' (ـتِ), in the plural form. ﴿And fear Allah﴾, so do not disobey Him and do not oppose His command, ﴿that you may receive mercy﴾.

[Akhbaranā 'Abd al-Wāḥid ibn Aḥmad al-Malīḥī] [[What is between the two brackets is missing from "A".]], akhbaranā Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥusayn ibn Aḥmad al-Mukhlidī, akhbaranā Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq al-Sarrāj, ḥaddathanā Qutayba ibn Saʿīd, ḥaddathanā al-Layth, from ʿUqayl, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim: he does not wrong him, nor does he humiliate him. Whoever attends to the need of his brother, Allah attends to his need. Whoever relieves a Muslim of a distress, Allah will relieve him of a distress from the distresses of the Day of Resurrection. And whoever conceals a Muslim, Allah will conceal him on the Day of Resurrection." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Mazalim, chapter "The Muslim does not wrong the Muslim nor abandon him": 5/97, and Muslim in al-Birr wa al-Silah, chapter on the prohibition of wrongdoing, no. (2580): 4/1996, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/98.]]

In these two verses there is evidence that rebellion (baghy) does not remove the name of faith, because Allah the Exalted called them "brothers" and "believers" despite their being rebels. This is supported by what is related from al-Harith al-A'war, that ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu), who was the exemplar, was asked about fighting the people of rebellion, regarding the people of the Camel and Siffin: "Are they polytheists?" He said: "No, they fled from polytheism." It was said: "Are they hypocrites?" He said: "No, the hypocrites do not remember Allah except a little." It was said: "What is their status, then?" He said: "They are our brothers who rebelled against us." [[Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi related in his book "Ta'zim Qadr al-Salah": 2/543-544, three reports from ʿAli (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu), transmitted from him by Tariq ibn Shihab, Abu Wa'il, and Hakim ibn Jabir. See also: Minhaj al-Sunnah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Taymiyyah: 5/242-248, Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/323-324.]]

The baghi in the Sharia is one who rebels against a just imam. If a group gathers that has strength and power, refuses obedience to a just imam on a plausible interpretation (ta'wil), and appoints an imam of their own, then the ruling concerning them is that the imam sends to them and calls them to obey him. If they point to a grievance, he removes it from them; if they mention no grievance and persist in their rebellion, the imam fights them until they return to his obedience. Then the ruling in their fighting is that their fleeing one is not pursued, their captive is not killed, and their wounded is not finished off. On the day of the Camel, the caller of ʿAli (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu) proclaimed: "Beware: a fleeing one is not pursued, and a wounded one is not finished off." [[Related by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan as a statement of ʿAli: 8/181; al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2/155 declared it sound and al-Dhahabi agreed; Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd al-Razzaq and Saʿid ibn Mansur related it, and al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar declared it sound in Bulugh al-Maram. al-Hakim, al-Bayhaqi and al-Bazzar related it from Ibn Mas'ud as a marfu' report with a weak chain, in which is Kawthar ibn Hakim, who is abandoned (matruk). See: Nasb al-Rayah: 3/463, Talkhis al-Habir: 4/43, Subul al-Salam of al-San'ani: 3/259, Irwa' al-Ghalil: 8/113.]]

On the day of Siffin a captive was brought to ʿAli (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu), and he said to him: "I will not kill you in cold blood; indeed I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds."

And whatever one of the two groups destroys of the other's life or property during the fighting, there is no liability (ḍaman) upon it.

Ibn Shihab said: In that strife there were bloodshed in which the killer and the slain were known in some cases, and much property was destroyed. Then people reached a state where the war between them subsided and the ruling was applied to them; as far as I know, no one was subjected to retaliation (qisas) nor was anyone made to pay for property he had destroyed.

As for those in whom these three conditions do not all combine, namely that they are a small group without strength, or that they have no interpretation, or that they have not appointed an imam, they are not to be confronted so long as they do not take up fighting and do not attack the Muslims. If they do so, they are like highway robbers (qutta' al-tariq).

It is related that ʿAli (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu) heard a man saying in a corner of the mosque: "There is no judgment except for Allah, the Exalted." ʿAli said: "A word of truth by which falsehood is intended. You have three rights over us: we will not prevent you from Allah's mosques, that you mention the name of Allah in them; we will not withhold from you your share of the spoils (fay') as long as your hands are with our hands; and we will not begin fighting you." [[Related by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 8/184, connected through several chains; al-Shafi'i related it as a mursal report, saying: "Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It has reached us that ʿAli ..." Ibn Hajar said in Talkhis al-Habir: 4/45: "al-Shafi'i related it as mursal, and Ibn Abi Shaybah and al-Bayhaqi related it connected, and its origin is in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of ʿUbaydullah ibn Abi Rafi'." See also: Irwa' al-Ghalil of al-Albani: 8/117.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 49, verse 11:

And His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people﴾ to the end of the verse. Ibn 'Abbas said: It was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, because he had a deafness in his ear. Whenever he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the people had gotten ahead of him to the gathering, they would make room for him so that he could sit beside him and hear what he said. One day he came when he had missed [a rak'ah of the Fajr prayer] [[In "B" (two rak'ahs of the Fajr).]], and when the Prophet ﷺ finished the prayer, his companions took their seats, and each man was stingy with his place, so that hardly anyone would make room for another. Whenever a man came and found no place to sit, he would stand where he was. When Thabit finished the prayer, he came toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stepping over the necks of the people, saying: "Make room, make room!" They began making room for him until he reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with a man between him and the Prophet. He said to the man: "Make room." The man said: "You have found a place, so sit down." Thabit sat behind him, angry. When the darkness cleared, Thabit nudged the man and said: "Who is this?" He said: "I am so-and-so." Thabit said: "The son of such-and-such a woman," mentioning a mother of his for whom he had been reproached in the Jahiliyyah. The man lowered his head and was ashamed, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. [[Mentioned by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. (453).]]

Al-Dahhak said: It was revealed concerning the delegation of Banu Tamim that we mentioned, who used to mock the poor companions of the Prophet ﷺ, such as 'Ammar, Khabbab, Bilal, Suhayb, Salman, and Salim, mawla of Abu Hudhayfah, when they saw the shabbiness of their condition. So Allah the Exalted revealed concerning those among them who believed: ﴿O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule a people﴾, meaning men ridiculing men. [[Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr, 7/563, from Muqatil, and attributed by him to Ibn Abi Hatim.]] "Qawm" (people) is a noun that includes men and women, though it may be specific to a group of men: ﴿perhaps they may be better than them, nor let women [ridicule] women, perhaps they may be better than them﴾.

It is narrated from Anas that it was revealed concerning the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when they reproached Umm Salamah for her shortness [of stature]. [[Mentioned by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. (454).]]

And from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: it was revealed concerning Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab, when the women said to her: "A Jewess, daughter of two Jews." [[Mentioned by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. (454); al-Qurtubi, 16/326.]]

﴿Nor defame one another﴾, meaning: do not let some of you find fault with others, nor let some of you revile others. ﴿Nor call one another by [offensive] nicknames﴾. "Tanabuz" is the reciprocal form from "nabz," which is a nickname, namely calling a person by a name other than the one he was given.

'Ikrimah said: It is a man saying to a man: "O sinner! O hypocrite! O unbeliever!"

Al-Hasan said: A Jew or a Christian would accept Islam, and after his conversion he would be called "O Jew! O Christian!", so they were forbidden from that. [[Al-Tabari transmitted these two statements from 'Ikrimah and al-Hasan, 26/132-133, then said: "The most correct of the interpretations in my view is that Allah, dhikruhu, forbade the believers from calling one another by nicknames. Calling by nicknames is calling a person by what he dislikes, whether a name or an attribute. Allah's prohibition is general and does not single out some nicknames over others. It is not permissible for any Muslim to call his brother by a name or attribute he dislikes. Given this, all the statements that the people of interpretation have given, which we have mentioned, are sound, and none of them is more correct than another, since all of that is what Allah forbids the Muslims from, that some of them call others by offensive names."]]

'Ata' said: It is that you say to your brother: "O dog! O donkey! O pig!"

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Calling by nicknames" is that a man has committed sins, then repented of them, and he is forbidden to be reproached for what he did in the past. [[Transmitted by al-Tabari, 26/133; see also al-Durr al-Manthur, 7/564.]]

﴿Wretched is the name of defiance after faith.﴾ That is: wretched is the name of saying "O Jew!" or "O sinner!" to one who has believed and repented. It was also said that its meaning is: whoever does what is forbidden of mockery, defamation, and nicknaming is a sinner, and "wretched is the name of defiance after faith," so do not do that, lest you deserve the name of defiance. ﴿And whoever does not repent﴾ of that, ﴿those are the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿O you who believe, avoid much suspicion﴾. It was said: the verse was revealed concerning two men who backbit their companion. The reason was that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he went on a raid or a journey, would join a needy man to two wealthy men, who would serve them, going ahead to the lodging to prepare for them whatever food and drink suited them. On one of his journeys he joined Salman al-Farisi to two men. Salman went ahead to the lodging, but his eyes overcame him and he fell asleep, so he prepared nothing for them. When they arrived, they said to him: "Have you done nothing?" He said: "No, my eyes overcame me." They said to him: "Go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and ask him for food for us." Salman came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and asked him for food. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Go to Usama ibn Zayd and say to him: If he has any surplus of food and condiment, let him give it to you." Usama was the treasurer of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and in charge of his baggage. Salman came to him and said: "I have nothing." Salman returned to the two men and informed them. They said: "Usama had food, but he was stingy." So they sent Salman to a group of the Companions, but he found nothing with them. When he returned they said: "If we had sent you to the well of Sumayha, its water would have dried up." Then the two of them set off, spying, to see whether Usama had what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had ordered for them. When they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said to them: "What is it that I see the green of meat in your mouths?" They said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we have not eaten any meat today." He said: "Rather, you have been eating the flesh of Salman and Usama." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "O you who believe, avoid much suspicion." [[Cited by al-Qurtubi: 16/330-331.]] And it intends: that evil should not be assumed of people of goodness. ﴿Indeed, some suspicion is sin﴾. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Suspicion is of two kinds: one of them is sin, and it is that you suspect and speak of it; the other is not sin, and it is that you suspect but do not speak of it.

﴿And do not spy﴾. Tajassus (spying) is searching out the faults of people. Allah the Exalted forbade searching into what is concealed of people's affairs and pursuing their private faults, to the point that it becomes apparent what Allah has concealed of them.

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi related to us; Zahir ibn Ahmad related to us; Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi related to us; Abu Mus'ab related to us, from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of speech. Do not spy, do not compete (for worldly things), do not envy one another, do not hate one another, do not turn away from one another, and be, O servants of Allah, brothers." [[Related by al-Bukhari in al-Adab, chapter on "O you who believe, avoid much suspicion" (verse), 10/484; Muslim in al-Birr wa al-Silah, chapter on the prohibition of suspicion, no. (2563): 4/1985; and the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 13/109-110.]]

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tusi related to us with it; Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Isfarayini related to us; Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Isma'ili related to us; Abdullah ibn Nahiya related to us; Yahya ibn Aktham related to us; al-Fadl ibn Musa al-Shaybani related to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from Awfa ibn Dalham, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of those who believe with their tongues while faith has not reached their hearts: do not backbite the Muslims and do not pursue their faults, for whoever pursues the faults of the Muslims, Allah will pursue his fault, and whomever Allah pursues his fault, He will expose him, even within the interior of his mount."

He said: One day Ibn Umar looked at the Ka'ba and said: How great you are, and how great your sanctity is! Yet the believer is greater in sanctity before Allah than you. [[Related by al-Tirmidhi in al-Birr wa al-Silah, chapter on what has come concerning the honour of the believer: 6/180-181, and said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith; we do not know it except from the hadith of al-Husayn ibn Waqid. Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Samarqandi narrated something similar from Husayn ibn Waqid, and it has been narrated from Abu Barza al-Aslami from the Prophet (ﷺ) something similar to this." Also Imam Ahmad: 4/421, and the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 13/104. Abu Dawud related it in al-Adab, chapter on backbiting: 7/213-214, from Abu Barza al-Aslami, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Zayd ibn Wahb said: It was said to Ibn Mas'ud: "Would you like to see al-Walid ibn Uqba, whose beard drips with wine?" He said: "We have been forbidden from spying; if something becomes apparent to us, we will take him to account for it." [[Related by Abu Dawud in al-Adab, chapter on the prohibition of spying: 7/219; Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 10/232; and through al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 8/334.]]

﴿And let not some of you backbite others﴾. He says: let none of you speak ill of another in his absence with what would displease him regarding that which he is in.

Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharqi related to us; Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abdullah al-Taysafuni related to us; Abdullah ibn Umar al-Jawhari related to us; Ahmad ibn Ali al-Kushmihani related to us; Ali ibn Hujr related to us; Isma'il ibn Ja'far related to us, from al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayra that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you know what backbiting is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Your mentioning your brother with what he dislikes." It was said: "What if what I say is true of my brother?" He said: "If what you say is in him, you have backbitten him; and if what you say is not in him, you have slandered him." [[Related by Muslim in al-Birr wa al-Silah, chapter on the prohibition of backbiting, no. (2589): 4/2001; and the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 13/138-139.]] [136/b]

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tawba related to us; Abu al-Tahir al-Harithi related to us; Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kisa'i related to us; Abdullah ibn Mahmud related to us; Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khallal related to us; Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from al-Muthanna ibn al-Sabbah, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, that they mentioned a man in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "He does not eat until he is fed, and he does not travel until he is conveyed." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You have backbitten him." They said: "We only related what is in him." He said: "It is enough for you, when you mention your brother, to mention what is in him." [[Al-Mundhiri said in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib: 3/506: "Related by al-Asbahani with a hasan chain."]]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would hate it﴾. Mujahid said: When it was said to them, "Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother?" they said: "No." It was said: ﴿You would hate it﴾, meaning: just as you hate this, then avoid mentioning him with evil in his absence.

al-Zajjaj said: Its interpretation is: mentioning someone who is not present with evil is like eating the flesh of your brother while he is dead and does not perceive it.

Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Sharihi related to us; Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi related to us; Ibn Fanjawayh informed me; Ibn Abi Shayba related to us; al-Firyabi related to us; Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa related to us; Abu al-Mughira Abd al-Quddus ibn al-Hajjaj related to us; Safwan ibn Amr related to me; Rashid ibn Sa'd and Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr related to us, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When I was taken up (on the night journey), I passed by a people who had nails of copper with which they were scratching their faces and chests. I said: 'Who are these, O Jibril?' He said: 'These are the ones who eat the flesh of people and fall into their honour.'" [[Related by Abu Dawud in al-Adab, chapter on backbiting: 7/213; Abu Dawud's narration was described by al-Mundhiri as one in which some of its narrators related it as mursal; and Imam Ahmad: 3/224. Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir: 4/215 after quoting the hadith: "Abu Dawud alone related it."]] Maymun ibn Siyah [[In "A": Shayah; in "B": Sayyar. The correction is from "al-Tahdhib" and others.]] said: While I was sleeping, I suddenly saw the corpse of a black man, and a speaker saying: "Eat." I said: "O servant of Allah, why should I eat?" He said: "Because you backbitten the servant of so-and-so." I said: "By Allah, I did not mention anything good or bad about him." He said: "But you listened and were pleased with it." Thereafter Maymun would not backbite anyone, nor would he allow anyone to backbite anyone in his presence. [[See Hilyat al-Awliya: 3/107, where the last portion is mentioned from him.]]

﴿And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance, Merciful﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 49, verse 13:

﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female﴾ and so on. Ibn 'Abbas said: It was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays and his saying to a man who had not made room for him: "Son of so-and-so," reproaching him with his mother. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Who is it that mentions so-and-so?" Thabit said: "I am, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Look at the faces of the people." So he looked, and the Prophet said: "What did you see, Thabit?" He said: "I saw white, red and black." He said: "You do not excel them except in religion and piety." So this verse was revealed concerning Thabit, and concerning the man who had not made room: "O you who have believed, when you are told to make room in the gatherings, then make room" [[Mentioned by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 455; al-Qurtubi, 16/341. See also what precedes it, p. 343.]] [al-Mujadilah: 11].

Muqatil said: When the Day of the Conquest of Makkah came, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered Bilal to climb onto the roof of the Ka'bah and call the adhan. 'Attab ibn Asid ibn Abi al-'Is said: "Praise be to Allah who took my father before he saw this day." Al-Harith ibn Hisham said: "Has Muhammad not found anyone other than this black crow to be a muezzin?" Suhayl ibn 'Amr said: "If Allah wills something, He will change it." Abu Sufyan said: "I will not say anything, for I fear that the Lord of the heavens will inform Him of it." Then Jibril came and informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of what they had said. He summoned them and asked them about what they had said, and they admitted it. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse [[Ibid.]], and He restrained them from boasting of lineages, from piling up wealth, and from belittling the poor, saying:

﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female﴾, meaning Adam and Eve; that is, you are equal in lineage.

﴿And made you into peoples (shu'ub)﴾: the plural of sha'b, with the shin vowelled with a fatha. It refers to the major tribal groupings, such as Rabi'ah, Mudar, al-Aws and al-Khazraj. They were called shu'ub because of their branching out (tasha''ub) and their gathering together, like the branches of a tree (sha'ab ashjar al-shajar). The word sha'b is one of the words with contrary meanings (adhdad): it is said sha'aba, meaning he gathered, and sha'aba, meaning he separated.

﴿And tribes (qaba'il)﴾: these are below the shu'ub. Their singular is qabilah, such as Bakr from Rabi'ah and Tamim from Mudar. Below the qaba'il are the 'amair (sing. 'imarah, with the 'ayn vowelled with a fatha), such as Shaybān from Bakr and Darim from Tamim. Below the 'amair are the butun (sing. batn), such as Banu Ghalib and Lu'ayy of Quraysh. Below the butun are the afkhadh (sing. fakhdh), such as Banu Hashim and Umayyah from Banu Lu'ayy. Then come the fasa'il and the 'asha'ir (sing. fasilah and 'ashirah). There is no living group after the 'ashirah by which one may be described.

It has also been said: the shu'ub are from the non-Arabs ('ajam), the qaba'il are from the Arabs, and the asbat are from the Children of Israel.

Abu Rawq said: "The shu'ub" are those who do not ascribe themselves to anyone, but rather attribute themselves to cities and villages; "the qaba'il" are the Arabs who attribute themselves to their fathers.

﴿That you may know one another﴾: so that some of you may know others in closeness and distance of lineage, not so that you may boast. Then He informed them that the one of highest rank with Allah is the most pious among them, so He said:

﴿Indeed, the most noble of you with Allah is the most pious of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted﴾. Qatadah said concerning this verse: The noblest of nobility is piety, and the basest of baseness is immorality.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Haytham al-Turabi informed us: Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hamawayh informed us: Ibrahim ibn Khuzaym al-Shashi informed us: 'Abd ibn Humayd related to us: Yunus ibn Muhammad related to us: Sallam ibn Abi Muti' related to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Samurah ibn Jundub, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Lineage (al-hasab) is wealth, and nobility (al-karam) is piety." [[Related by al-Tirmidhi in Tafsir (Tafsir Surat al-Hujurat), 9/156-157, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib sahih hadith from the narration of Samurah; we do not know it except from the hadith of Sallam ibn Abi Muti'." Also by Ibn Majah in al-Zuhd, Bab al-Wara' wa al-Taqwa, no. 4219, 2/1410-1411; Imam Ahmad, 5/10; al-Hakim, 2/163 and 4/325, and he said: "This is a sahih hadith according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him; al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan, 7/136; and al-Daraqutni in al-Sunan, 3/302. He also has supporting narrations there from Abu Hurayrah in the same place. See also Irwa' al-Ghalil, 6/271-272; Fath al-Bari, 9/135.]]

Ibn 'Abbas said: The nobility of this world is wealth, and the nobility of the Hereafter is piety.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Haytham informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hamawayh informed us: Ibrahim ibn Khuzaym informed us: 'Abd ibn Humayd related to us: al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad informed us, from Musa ibn 'Ubaydah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Umar, that the Prophet (ﷺ) circumambulated on the Day of the Conquest upon his mount, touching the corners with his staff. When he came out, he did not find a place to kneel his mount, so he descended onto the hands of men. Then he stood and addressed them, praising Allah and extolling Him, and he said: "Praise be to Allah, who has removed from you the arrogance of the Jahiliyyah and its pride in ancestors. People are of two kinds: a righteous, pious one who is noble before Allah, and a wicked, miserable one who is contemptible before Allah." Then he recited: "O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female." Then he said: "I say this word of mine and I ask Allah's forgiveness for myself and for you." [[Related by al-Tirmidhi in Tafsir, 9/155-156, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it except from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar from Ibn 'Umar, and only through this route. 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far is weak; Yahya ibn Ma'in and others declared him weak, and he is the father of 'Ali ibn al-Madini." Also related by 'Abd ibn Humayd in al-Muntakhab min al-Musnad, pp. 253-254, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 13/124, where he said: "This is a gharib hadith." al-Suyuti added in al-Durr al-Manthur, 7/579, that it is attributed to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh.]]

'Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us: Muhammad, who is Ibn Salam [folio 137a], related to us: 'Abdah related to us, from 'Ubayd Allah, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Who among the people is the most noble?" He said: "The most noble of them before Allah is the most pious of them." They said: "We are not asking you about this." He said: "Then the most noble of people is Yusuf, the Prophet of Allah, son of the Prophet of Allah, son of the Prophet of Allah, son of the Friend of Allah." They said: "We are not asking you about this." He said: "Then are you asking me about the mines of the Arabs?" They said: "Yes." He said: "The best of you in the Jahiliyyah are the best of you in Islam, when they gain understanding." [[Related by al-Bukhari in al-Anbiya', Bab Qawl Allah Ta'ala (wa-ittakhadha Allahu Ibrahima khalilan), 6/387; and Muslim in al-Fada'il, Bab min Fada'il Yusuf 'alayhi al-salam, no. 2378, 4/1846-1847.]]

Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir informed us: 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan related to us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj related to us: 'Amr al-Naqid related to us: Kathir ibn Hisham related to us: Ja'far ibn Burqan related to us, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah does not look at your forms or your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds." [[Related by Muslim in al-Birr wa al-Silah, Bab Tahrim Zulm al-Muslim wa Khadhlihi, no. 2564, 4/1986-1987; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 14/340-341.]]

The Almighty's words: ﴿The Bedouin say, "We have believed"﴾ — the verse. It was revealed concerning a group from the clan of Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah, who came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a year of drought. They displayed Islam, but they were not believers in secret. They fouled the roads of Madinah with filth, and they raised its prices. They would come and go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and say: "The Arabs have come to you with themselves, on the backs of their mounts, but we have come to you with our baggage, our dependants and our offspring. We did not fight you as Banu so-and-so and Banu so-and-so fought you." They were putting the Prophet ﷺ under obligation, seeking charity, and saying, "Give us." So Allah revealed this verse concerning them [[See: Tafsir of Abd al-Razzaq: 2/235; al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/117; al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/585; al-Qurtubi: 16/348.]].

al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning the Bedouins whom Allah mentioned in Surat al-Fath, namely the Bedouins of Juhaynah, Muzaynah, Aslam, Ashja' and Ghifar. They used to say, "We have believed," so that they would be safe for their own selves and their wealth. When they were called to march out to al-Hudaybiyah, they stayed behind. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed "The Bedouin say, 'We have believed.'" [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/117; al-Qurtubi: 16/348.]] — meaning, "We affirm (sadaqna)."

﴿Say: You have not believed, but say, "We have submitted,"﴾ — meaning, we yielded and surrendered, out of fear of killing and captivity. ﴿For faith has not yet entered your hearts.﴾ So He informed that the reality of faith is affirmation by the heart, and that acknowledgement by the tongue and the outward performance of its laws by the bodies does not constitute faith without affirmation by the heart and sincerity.

Abu al-Wahid al-Malihi related to us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi related to us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, Muhammad ibn Ghurayr al-Zuhri related to us, Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to us, from his father, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Amir ibn Sa'd informed me, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave to a group of people while I was sitting among them. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ left out a man among them and did not give to him, though he was the most beloved of them to me. So I stood up to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [and spoke to him privately] [[Omitted from "B".]], and I said: "What is the matter with you regarding so-and-so? By Allah, I think he is a believer." He said: "Or a Muslim?" He said: So he was silent for a little while, then what I knew of him overcame me, and I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the matter with you regarding so-and-so? By Allah, I think he is a believer." He said: "Or a Muslim." He said: "Indeed I give to a man while another is more beloved to me than him, out of fear that he will be thrown face-first into the Fire." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in az-Zakat, chapter on the saying of Allah, "They do not ask people importunately" (2:273): 3/340, and in al-Iman 1/79. Also Muslim in al-Musafirin, chapter on winning over the hearts of those who fear for their faith because of its weakness, and the prohibition of asserting faith without conclusive evidence, no. 150: 1/132.]]

Islam is entry into peace (al-silm), and it is submission and obedience. It is said: "aslama al-rajul" (the man "entered into peace") when he entered into that state, just as it is said "ashta al-rajul" (he entered winter) when he entered winter, "asāfa" (he entered summer) when he entered summer, and "arba'a" (he entered spring) when he entered spring. Thus, some Islam is obedience in the true sense, by the tongue, the bodies and the heart, like the Almighty's saying to Ibrahim, peace be upon him: ﴿"Submit," he said, "I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 131]. And some Islam is submission by the tongue without the heart, and that is His saying: ﴿But say, "We have submitted," for faith has not yet entered your hearts.﴾

﴿And if you obey Allah and His Messenger﴾ — outwardly and inwardly, secretly and openly. Ibn Abbas said: "Make your faith sincere." ﴿He will not deprive you﴾ — Abu Amr read "ya'litkum" with an alif, in accordance with His saying: ﴿And We did not deprive them﴾ [al-Tur: 21], while the others read it without an alif. Both are dialects, and their meaning is: He will not diminish you. It is said: "alita yalitu alta" and "lata yaliitu laytan," meaning he diminished. ﴿Anything of your deeds﴾ — meaning He will not diminish anything from the reward of your deeds. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.﴾

Then He explained the reality of faith, saying: ﴿The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then have not doubted﴾ meaning, they have not been in doubt about their religion, ﴿and have striven with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah. Those are the truthful﴾ in their faith.

When these two verses were revealed, the Bedouin Arabs came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), swearing by Allah that they were believers and truthful, while Allah knew otherwise about them. So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed:

﴿Say: Would you inform Allah about your religion?﴾ The word "ta'lim" (instruction, here meaning informing) is used here in the sense of "i'lam" (informing), and for this reason He said "bi-dinikum" and introduced the particle "ba'" (with) into it. The meaning is: Would you inform Allah of your religion that you hold? ﴿But Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and Allah is All-Knowing of everything﴾, He has no need of your informing Him.

﴿They consider it a favour to you that they have embraced Islam. Say: Do not consider your Islam a favour to me; rather, Allah has conferred a favour upon you that He has guided you to faith﴾ meaning: by your embracing Islam. In the codex of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) it reads "idh hadakum li-l-iman" (that He guided you to faith). ﴿If you are truthful﴾, that you are believers.

﴿Indeed, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾ Ibn Kathir read "ya'malun" with the letter ya', while the others read it with the letter ta'.
